checks: The own uniform measure is a log-concave submeasure by Brunn–Minkowski, and a containing halfspace bounds the mass by M. Total mass is continuous in the weak topology of measures supported on fixed compact K.

For any closed H, an outward-shifted open halfspace G_δ contains H and lies inside the shifted closed H_δ. Portmanteau and finite continuity from above preserve the exact closed constraints, including whole fibers on vertical boundaries.
For compact sets A,B, their open δ-neighborhoods combine into the closed δ-neighborhood of (1−t)A+tB. Compact inner approximation gives the open-set log-concavity inequality.

The closed upper and open lower weak-limit inequalities preserve this comparison as δ decreases to zero. The limit may be singular, and positivity of the maximum follows from the feasible full own-fiber mass.

overlap.comparison: The accepted many-fiber selector is a dominated submeasure with a prescribed mass and centroid restriction. This candidate maximizes mass under halfspace domination on one fixed fiber and admits singular log-concave limits.
The accepted retained-mass optimizer has an explicit density bound and a centroid constraint, neither of which defines this class.

readability: The proof uses the multiplicative compact-set definition in the relative fiber plane, including lower-dimensional support.
summary: Weak compactness and closure of both halfspace domination and log-concavity prove the asserted attainment, including singular limits.
